overview: I’m documenting my homelab: a hands-on environment for networking practice and testing, with room for future server and service hosting. This is a tour of my equipment and how it connects. Setup guides, troubleshooting, and lessons learned live on the blog.

equipment.description: ISP equipment providing the fiber connection to the home network. Detailed setup documentation has not been recorded.

The primary household router remains in place, with the Cisco lab behind the existing home network so lab configuration changes do not disrupt household connectivity. A summarized route for the lab networks will be added to the home router after the C1111 is installed.

The planned lab router will connect the existing home network to the Cisco lab. The first implementation uses router-on-a-stick: the C1111 will provide Layer 3 routing and a default gateway for each lab VLAN, while the 3560CX initially operates primarily at Layer 2. Router configuration has not begun.

equipment.description: Inspected and validated through console access before configuration. Hardware, interfaces, IOS, licensing, and PoE were verified. Hostname and baseline configuration, VLAN creation, management SVI, management access port, and SSH preparation are complete. GigabitEthernet0/9 is reserved as the planned 802.1Q trunk toward the C1111.
specifications: 8 × Gigabit Ethernet PoE+ access ports · 240W available PoE budget
2 × additional Gigabit copper uplink interfaces · SFP uplink capability

equipment.description: A compact, low-power system intended as the lab’s future compute and server platform. Integration into the lab environment is planned; no server software installation is documented.

topology.alt: Provisional topology: Internet → Fiber ONT → Nighthawk RAX45 home router → Cisco C1111-4P lab router → Cisco Catalyst WS-C3560CX-8PC-S switch → HP EliteDesk 800 G6 Mini / future lab compute and future lab devices. Household computers and IoT devices branch from the RAX45. The C1111 has not arrived; lab uplinks, routing, and server deployment remain planned.
